body.p: . src/xslt_ast_internal.h, internal, after and the IR unit ().

item.p: One AST per stylesheet (a used package is another): modules, nodes, attributes, expressions, static contexts, a declaration list, name tokens, namespace bindings and URIs, text; index-addressed arrays with entry 0 "none" that grow through an allocator while the reader builds and are sealed before lowering (as sxml_ir_unit). Module URIs get their own allocations, so the per-expression sxml_ast borrows them as source name. The AST owns those ASTs and a reference to each module's document node.

Nodes: one kind per XSLT 4.0 element in the 4.0 schema (schema-for-xslt40.xsd; xsl:transform is STYLESHEET, xsl:note never arrives), plus LITERAL_RESULT_ELEMENT, TEXT_NODE, EXTENSION_INSTRUCTION, UNKNOWN_INSTRUCTION (forwards-compatible) and DATA_ELEMENT. A node's attributes are consecutive; children linked as in .

Attributes: one kind per attribute name of the schema; the value is read into the form the element syntax names: EXPRESSION, PATTERN, VALUE_TEMPLATE, SEQUENCE_TYPE, ITEM_TYPE (each its own sxml_ast), TEXT, BOOLEAN, NUMBER, KEYWORD, NAME, NAME_LIST, NAMESPACE_BINDING. QName-valued attributes are resolved while reading (XTSE0280); names inside expressions stay as written for static analysis. An AVT is always a VALUE_TEMPLATE, even without {: an XPath AST with a STRING_TEMPLATE body, lowered as string templates are. Standard attributes stay as TEXT; their effect is in the static context.

Static context per element, resolved and shared until something changes: statically known namespaces (after fixed-namespaces), xpath default namespace (or ##any), default collation, mode and validation, expand-text, version, cumulative excluded and extension namespaces, static base URI. Lowering never walks up the tree.

Reader duties (4.5): whitespace and commentary stripping, use-when, shadow attributes, simplified stylesheets (synthesized STYLESHEET and TEMPLATE match "."; expand-text from the version, 3.7), include and import read in place depth first (duplicate includes in a level ignored, 4.0), syntax of every value. Import precedence is computed by sxml_xslt_ast_seal from the module tree (post-order, includes share their includer's), since modules are added in pre-order.

Who writes what: the builder and lifecycle functions are defined in a new src/xslt_ast.c with tests/xslt_ast_test.c, both written by packet (the AST's only producer, as 1.16 wrote xpath_ast.c); added to 4.5's files in docs/tasks/phase-4.md. A text form (sxml_xslt_ast_write_text) serves golden tests; the header writes out for-each-group-001, a template rule and an xsl:function in it.

Rejected: one shared sxml_ast for all expressions (its capacity is fixed from one concrete syntax tree, ); keeping attribute values as text for lowering to parse (every lowering part would repeat the checks, and XTSE errors belong to reading); a fixed-capacity AST sized from the trees (modules arrive one by one through the resolver).
